rationale:
The issue dart-lang/core#340 reports a type cast crash ('Null' is not a subtype of type 'String') when CancelableOperation.then invokes onValue after cancellation. The minimized production patch adds a single conjunct `&& !isCanceled` to prevent onValue from executing when the operation was canceled, directly addressing the reported crash path. The trigger test 'after completing with a future does not invoke `onValue`' uses expectAsync1 with count: 0 to assert onValue is never called when a completer is completed with a Future, then canceled before the Future resolves—exactly the scenario described in the issue. The strict_post_minimization validation confirms this test fails on buggy (5737ad7) and passes on fixed (b7cf894) with deterministic reproduction across 3 repetitions. The second test 'after the value is completed invokes `onValue`' verifies the non-buggy path still works when cancel occurs after a non-Future value completes. No formatting, refactor, feature extension, documentation-only, or test infrastructure changes are present in the minimized production patch. The active_same_project_root_causes list is empty, so no duplicate exists within dart-archive/async.

The issue dart-lang/core#340 reports a concrete crash (`type 'Null' is not a subtype of type 'String' in type cast`) when calling `then()` on a `CancelableOperation` followed by `cancel()`. The stack trace pinpoints cancelable_operation.dart:106, which matches the patched line. The minimized production patch adds a single guard `&& !isCanceled` to prevent invoking `onValue` with a null result when the operation was canceled after completion. The trigger test 'after completing with a future does not invoke `onValue`' reproduces the exact scenario described in the issue: completing with a Future, canceling, then completing the underlying Future. Strict runtime evidence confirms this test fails deterministically on buggy revision 5737ad76 and passes on fixed revision b7cf8945. The patch contains no formatting, documentation, or unrelated logic changes—only the minimal conditional fix. The trigger tests use only pre-existing APIs (`CancelableCompleter`, `complete`, `cancel`, `isCanceled`) available in the parent revision, requiring no new production API. No active same-project root causes were supplied, confirming no duplication.
